svg.title: What USPS says about Package Pickup and Pickup on Demand: cost, timing, cutoff, limits, postage, the DMM stamp rule and what happens after scheduling.
svg.text: USPS Package Pickup
What USPS's pages say
Package Pickup (free)
Free, however many items are scheduled.
Next delivery day or a day you choose,
at the time the carrier delivers mail.
Schedule, edit or cancel until 2:00 AM
Central Time on the day (Mon to Sat).
Pickup on Demand (fee)
A fee per trip (listed in Notice 123).
A two-hour window you choose.
Schedule, edit or cancel until 5:00 AM
local time on the day (Mon to Sat).
Limits
Each item: up to 70 pounds and 130
inches in length and girth. Postage
prepaid before pickup. Not all addresses
are eligible. If stamps are the only
postage and the item is over 10 oz or
over 1/2 inch thick, it may not be picked
up: take it to a Post Office (DMM).
Hazardous, fragile, liquid
FAQ: hazardous materials must meet DMM
or IMM standards. The FAQ does not say
if fragile or liquid items count as
hazardous; DMM 601 has separate
packaging rules for each.
After you schedule
Up to 6 months ahead. Leave the package
where you chose; you need not be there.
Snow, ice, blocked paths or dogs may
prevent a pickup.
Sources: USPS FAQ, USPS.com (no update dates);
